text: Cole says the durable content library matters more than any one platform hit.
Tweets are positioned as the smallest training unit for clear and memorable writing.
Atomic essays are defined as roughly 300-word visual essays that can be drafted in about 30 minutes.
The atomic essay trains headlines, hooks, formatting, rhythm, and bulleted lists together.
Carousels add visual sequencing and tighter per-slide constraints to the writing stack.
Cole argues that list-shaped, actionable ideas fit carousels better than nuanced or long-winded topics.
AI may reduce production friction, but the operator still owns taste, image choice, and visual assembly.
Articles are framed as reusable long-form anchors that can be compressed, expanded, republished, or performed.
Cole describes the library as owned material that can be cut apart, recombined, or moved between free and paid contexts.
Prompts are presented as reusable assets for personal work, marketing, and digital products.
The operator must first acquire and articulate a skill before automating a bounded part of it.
Cole closes by treating useful prompts and systems built for oneself as potential products.
The five formats operate as a skill and leverage progression, not merely a list of unrelated channels.
